children: Chinese self-driving technology company Momenta is partnering with Dongfeng Stellantis Automotive Technology to provide advanced driver assistance systems for Peugeot and Jeep production models.

The driver assistance systems will be introduced in China, Europe and other global markets, Momenta said in a statement Monday, without providing a time frame. Dongfeng Stellantis is a joint venture established by Dongfeng Motor, Stellantis and other partners.

The global strategic partnership, which was signed on Thursday, will use Momenta's R7 world model for driving assistance, the company said. Under the partnership, Peugeot and Jeep will work closely with Momenta on providing intelligent driving to users.

The collaboration comes as more global automakers turn to Chinese technology companies to accelerate the rollout of advanced driver-assistance features, with Chinese automakers leading the deployment of such features.
For Stellantis, the partnership also ties to a broader effort to use its China operations to develop vehicles for markets beyond China.

The move also marks Momenta's continued efforts to expand its services beyond China. The company previously partnered with international automotive suppliers including Valeo to develop driving-assistance and autonomous driving products for China and other markets.

Momenta listed in Hong Kong in July, after pricing its shares at 295.60 Hong Kong dollars each and raising about HK$5.9 billion in its initial public offering. Its shares were last down 5.9% at HK$151.10 in afternoon trading Monday.
The company's shares have been under pressure, showing investors' concerns about the pace at which self-driving companies can turn their technology to sustained revenue and profits.
